answer: In an agent market coordinating a voyage from a wharf, each trading identity must lock a refundable bond for 30 days before receiving a fixed order quota. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 1,000 bonds; splitting one bond cannot multiply access. Even at the zenith of demand, quotas remain bond-backed, so a sybil swarm costs real capital and its foregone returns rather than merely the price of generating new keys.
